[Buhler and Koblitz (1998)](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bulletin-of-the-australian-mathematical-society/article/lattice-basis-reduction-jacobi-sums-and-hyperelliptic-cryptosystems/211979CB954028EF8899B3FB49930091)

attack, not an assumed classical dominance theorem. No balanced row is ever
selected by comparing it to the true Jacobi sum. Failure to find such a row
returns UNKNOWN, not a negative result or evidence of quantum advantage.

notes.text:
# Exact Surface Counts: CM Reconstruction And A Real Classical Attack

2026-10-17. Local mathematical derivations, review pending. No novelty claim.

**Superseding classical comparison:** the [known-norm reduction](JACOBI_KNOWN_NORM_REDUCTION.md)
identifies a published deterministic polynomial-time classical recovery
theorem that applies to the public ideal AND known relative norm. Under the
stated Jacobi/primary identities this removes the prime-conductor asymptotic
quantum opening, without needing a uniform LLL success theorem. Its actual
theorem inputs are constructed and checked; the imported recovery algorithm
is not implemented here. This page retains the original experiment and real
LLL results, not a current claim that quantum PIP is needed.

## Research Decision

The preceding HDQI source remained unresolved. We compared independent routes:

- The new [lattice Gaussian sampler](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20133) offers a
  quadratic improvement, not an identified polynomial lattice breakthrough.
- Curve point counting is NOT a new opening:
  [Kedlaya](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0411623) already gives quantum polynomial time
  in genus and log field size. We rejected a proposed Fermat-curve application
  as rediscovery before implementation.
- Exact Jacobi reconstruction from compact number-field data is a different
  mechanism from preparing a hard interference source. [Tal's modular
  factorial preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29453) uses known quantum
  principal-ideal/unit methods and phase disambiguation for repeated-character
  sums. [Biasse and Song](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02280) provide the underlying
  S-unit framework. These are external research results, not repo routines.

Selected question: can that arithmetic yield a charged exact point-count
reduction for split Fermat SURFACES, and what can a serious classical attack
already reconstruct? This is a candidate reduction experiment, not a new
end-to-end quantum implementation or a refutation of the cited papers.

## Problem, Input And Intended Advantage

Count projective solutions over F_p of

    X^d + Y^d + Z^d = W^d,      p prime, d>=3, d|(p-1).

p and d are public binary integers. A verified order-d root eta in F_p is
public, not a hidden function. The character is defined by
chi(x)=zeta_d^j when x^((p-1)/d)=eta^j; a table of size d, not p, implements
this evaluator. The EXHAUSTIVE native reference additionally makes a size-p
table, explicitly charged and never used by the public-ideal attack.

The proposed quantum target is polynomial in d and log p, NOT polynomial
in log d. To get a polynomial succinct-input algorithm, require an explicit
growth promise d=poly(log p). Fixed d already has strong classical arithmetic
methods and cannot establish an asymptotic separation. No classical lower
bound or best-known-algorithm separation is claimed for growing d here.

The prospective mechanism is a carry-described cyclotomic ideal, a real
principal-ideal/unit reconstruction, exact local residues and an integer
point-count lift. No coherent hidden oracle, source preparation assumption
or free full-field sum is part of that proposed pipeline. The quantum
principal-ideal/unit routines and generic three-character extension have
NOT been implemented or independently reviewed by this pass.

## Exact Reduction

Let J(a,b,c)=sum_(x+y+z=1) chi^a(x)chi^b(y)chi^c(z), extending ALL characters
by zero at0. For a,b,c in1..d-1 with a+b+c !=0 mod d,

    #surface = p^2+p+1 + C,
    C = sum_(admissible ordered triples) J(a,b,c).

Character orthogonality gives this projective formula. The number of terms is
B=(d-1)(d^2-3d+3), and each has absolute value p. Thus |C|<=Bp. C is an
integer, not an approximate complex number. If p>2B, C mod p^2 has a unique
lift in [-Bp,Bp]. If p<=2B=O(d^3), a full-field classical convolution count
costs polynomial time in d. The prototype rejects ambiguous residues rather
than silently using centered rounding. It explicitly counts the projective
boundary, not just the affine chart.

All triple sums are computed by exact two-character sums and a convolution
identity. When a+b=0, the missing zero-convolution mass matters:
J(a,-a,c)=p*chi^a(-1). Dropping it changes the norm and the point count.

## Ideal And Valuation Conventions

Use K=Q(zeta_d), the monic cyclotomic integral basis, and POSITIVE reductions
zeta_d -> eta^t, t in(Z/dZ)^*. The generalized Stickelberger carry profile is

    e_t = 2-floor(((at mod d)+(bt mod d)+(ct mod d))/d).

It satisfies e_t+e_(-t)=2 and sum e_t=phi(d). The inverse-root convention
has complementary carries; copying its labels would be wrong. Every native
sum is checked at all split primes modulo p^3, including exact valuations2.
Teichmuller roots use eta_t^(p^(h-1)) mod p^h. The exact relative norm is
J*conjugate(J)=p^2 in the FIELD, not merely a floating magnitude at one place.

To reduce J/p^v to h unit digits requires h+v input digits. The native helper
demonstrates this and rejects inversion of p modulo p^h. It does NOT implement
valuation-aware division of arbitrary compact quantum outputs. That bit-cost
extension is still an explicit obligation; known repeated-character residue
theorems must not silently be treated as arbitrary three-character routines.

## Strong Classical Baseline: Public Ideal LLL

This deliberately instantiates established classical arithmetic rather than
claiming LLL/Jacobi reconstruction as new:
[Buhler and Koblitz (1998)](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bulletin-of-the-australian-mathematical-society/article/lattice-basis-reduction-jacobi-sums-and-hyperelliptic-cryptosystems/211979CB954028EF8899B3FB49930091)
gives a fixed-small-conductor algorithm polynomial in log p. Standard
[odd-prime Jacobi primary congruences](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/82645)
also predate this project; the three-character form below has a local proof.

We build the actual ideal lattice using ONLY public p,d,eta and carries:
coefficient rows satisfy A(eta_t)=0 mod p^e_t. Sequential modular kernels
have checked determinant p^phi(d). LLL returns rows which are tested for
A*conjugate(A)=p^2. Ideal membership plus that norm gives equality of
principal ideals. Kronecker's theorem then leaves only a root of unity.

All64 selected small-input ideals yield a balanced row. This is an actual
attack, not an assumed classical dominance theorem. No balanced row is ever
selected by comparing it to the true Jacobi sum. Failure to find such a row
returns UNKNOWN, not a negative result or evidence of quantum advantage.

## Prime Conductors Need No Phase Oracle

For odd prime conductor ell, lambda=1-zeta_ell, the THREE-character sum obeys

    J(a,b,c) = 1 mod lambda^2.

Elementary derivation: expand zeta^e=1-e*lambda modulo lambda^2. The number
of nonzero triples summing to1 is p^2-3p+3, congruent to1 mod ell. For any
one coordinate, fixing x!=1 leaves p-2 choices for the other two; at x=1
there are p-1, but log_chi(1)=0. The total linear coefficient is therefore
divisible by ell, since sum_(x!=0) log_chi(x) is divisible by ell for odd ell.
As ell is divisible by lambda^(ell-1), both required congruences follow.

In Z[zeta_ell]/lambda^2, test A(1)=1 and A'(1)=0 mod ell. The2ell roots of
unity have distinct residues in this quotient. Thus this primary condition
selects the correct root multiple of a balanced generator CLASSICALLY, with
no phase estimate or true character sum. It does not replace norm
normalization: multiplying by the non-root unit1+zeta_5 preserves the ideal
but fails the relative-norm test. Composite conductors are not covered by
this implemented primary-normalization proof.

## Live End-To-End Classical Result

LLL plus primary normalization reproduces all six prime-conductor native
surface controls. More importantly, at

    p=2305843009213693951, d=11,
    #surface=5316911983139663865501362488876572959.

The public computation uses51 distinct ideal profiles for200 symmetric
triple records. NO p-sized table, true Jacobi sum or phase oracle is used.
The tests independently replay norm, ideal membership, determinant/index,
primary congruences, complete multiplicities, rationality and the Weil bound
without rerunning LLL. This is a checkable algebraic certificate under the
stated local derivation, NOT an independently enumerated 61-bit field or
formal theorem proof. No worst-case growing-conductor LLL success theorem
has been established. In particular, a finite classical success is not a
general dequantization. Cubic controls are explicitly already classical:
#surface=p^2+7p+1 for the split primes, not a quantum benchmark.

Fourteen native small-field controls retain1032 symmetric triple records,
64 selected ideal attacks and246 synthetic coarse-phase checks. The latter
only calibrate root spacing; no quantum phase estimation was executed and
prime-conductor primary normalization makes those checks unnecessary for
the implemented public reconstruction.

## Reproduce And Next Scientific Work

Run `python theorems/jacobi_surface_reconstruction.py --write` and
`python -m pytest tests/test_jacobi_surface_reconstruction.py -q`.

That next question has now been answered at the appropriate theorem level:
known-norm recovery, not unproved uniform LLL success, is the classical
baseline. Read JACOBI_KNOWN_NORM_REDUCTION.md and run its separate producer.
Independent review of the local application is still needed. Do not spend
another pass scanning primes or implementing known quantum PIP for this
prime-conductor proposal. A broader arithmetic candidate must first specify
an output not already supplied by the known-ideal/known-norm theorem; unknown
norms and composite root ambiguities are not automatically quantum openings.
No central candidate/general negative or groundbreaking algorithm is claimed.

notes.result:
The [surface experiment](JACOBI_SURFACE_RECONSTRUCTION.md) proposed quantum
principal-ideal/unit recovery from public Jacobi carries. Generic principal
ideal problems can be hard. But this input also supplies the exact relative
norm, J*bar(J)=p^2. That additional information changes the computational
problem. Comparing only generic PIP or empirical LLL success misses the
appropriate classical competitor.

[Lenstra and Silverberg, Testing isomorphism of lattices over CM-orders,
1706.07373v3](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.07373), Theorem 1.3, gives a
deterministic classical polynomial-time decision AND recovery algorithm for
an ideal and prescribed relative norm in a CM-order, when the polarized
ideal identity holds. No GRH assumption is part of that theorem. Its
Algorithms 18.6/18.7 establish the recovery assertion, not merely a test of
the principal-ideal class. The factorization in Algorithm 18.1 is of a
constructed integer with bounded small prime factors, not a free generic
integer-factorization oracle.

**Decision:** for odd prime conductor and the stated public split-root
input, this published theorem plus the Jacobi identities and primary
congruence gives classical polynomial-time exact surface counting in
ell and log p. The proposed asymptotic quantum advantage is therefore not
a credible target under those premises. Do not continue this route by
searching for LLL failures or implementing known quantum PIP primitives.
This is a prior-art application, NOT a new classical algorithm claim.
notes.self_check:
- **Wrong theorem problem?** Theorem 1.3 requires the norm, not just the
  ideal. Here the norm is exactly the public scalar p^2. If the application
  supplied only an unknown positive unit times p^2, this reduction would
  fail. Native checks and the Jacobi Weil identity rule that out here.
- **Invalid ideal/involution?** Carry orientation matters. Every product
  ideal is checked exactly, and inverse-label inputs are retained as distinct
  valid inputs, not confused with the intended J. A carry or ideal-identity
  counterexample would invalidate the local application.
- **Norm identity implies existence?** It does not in general. This family
  has a concrete Jacobi witness analytically; arbitrary polarized ideals
  cannot inherit the YES conclusion. Native small witnesses independently
  check that premise but are not a proof for all inputs.
- **Uncharged number-theory oracle?** A verified eta is part of both input
  models; neither algorithm gets a hidden root for free. The imported
  theorem is unconditional deterministic polynomial time in its explicit
  input size, not a heuristic unit-group/PIP subroutine. Efficient public
  ideal construction and polynomial output size are shown above.
- **Root ambiguity still hard?** Prime-primary normalization removes it
  without evaluating J. This pass does NOT extend that step to all composite
  conductors. A counterexample to the prime-primary proof would reopen
  exact identification, not make generic normalized recovery quantum-hard.
- **Does this refute a recent quantum paper?** No. The repo's specific
  prime-conductor surface target is narrower than external claims and may
  have different output/input conventions. No author-error conclusion is
  inferred from a missing citation or this local reduction alone.

notes.text:
# Known Relative Norm Removes The Prime-Conductor Quantum Opening

2026-10-17. Published classical theorem, local application REVIEW PENDING.
This supersedes the suggestion that growing-conductor LLL success is the
decisive unresolved question for this particular surface-counting proposal.
It does not assert that a Gentry-Szydlo implementation exists in the repo.

## Question And Decision

The [surface experiment](JACOBI_SURFACE_RECONSTRUCTION.md) proposed quantum
principal-ideal/unit recovery from public Jacobi carries. Generic principal
ideal problems can be hard. But this input also supplies the exact relative
norm, J*bar(J)=p^2. That additional information changes the computational
problem. Comparing only generic PIP or empirical LLL success misses the
appropriate classical competitor.

[Lenstra and Silverberg, Testing isomorphism of lattices over CM-orders,
1706.07373v3](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.07373), Theorem 1.3, gives a
deterministic classical polynomial-time decision AND recovery algorithm for
an ideal and prescribed relative norm in a CM-order, when the polarized
ideal identity holds. No GRH assumption is part of that theorem. Its
Algorithms 18.6/18.7 establish the recovery assertion, not merely a test of
the principal-ideal class. The factorization in Algorithm 18.1 is of a
constructed integer with bounded small prime factors, not a free generic
integer-factorization oracle.

**Decision:** for odd prime conductor and the stated public split-root
input, this published theorem plus the Jacobi identities and primary
congruence gives classical polynomial-time exact surface counting in
ell and log p. The proposed asymptotic quantum advantage is therefore not
a credible target under those premises. Do not continue this route by
searching for LLL failures or implementing known quantum PIP primitives.
This is a prior-art application, NOT a new classical algorithm claim.

## Direct Reduction To Theorem 1.3

Inputs: odd prime ell, prime p with ell|(p-1), explicit order-ell eta mod p,
and admissible nontrivial character exponents a,b,c with a+b+c nonzero mod ell.
Use A=Z[zeta_ell] and the POSITIVE embeddings zeta -> eta^t. All data are
explicit integers; no coherent oracle, true Jacobi value or field-sized
character table is an input.

1. A is a CM-order. In the basis 1,zeta,...,zeta^(ell-2), the multiplication
   table and conjugation matrix have polynomial size and integer entries.
2. Build I from the public split-prime powers P_t^e_t, with
   e_t=2-floor(((at mod ell)+(bt mod ell)+(ct mod ell))/ell).
   A basis follows from modular evaluation kernels at the lifted split roots.
3. Conjugation sends P_t to P_(-t). Since e_t+e_(-t)=2, we have
   I*bar(I)=product_t P_t^2=p^2*A. Set w=p^2, a totally positive scalar.
4. The Jacobi ideal identity gives I=(J); the Weil identity gives
   J*bar(J)=p^2. These establish the YES promise. IMPORTANT: the identity
   I*bar(I)=w*A by itself is NOT a proof that a normalized generator exists.
5. The published algorithm returns v with I=A*v and v*bar(v)=p^2.
   The ratio v/J is an algebraic unit with relative norm1. Every embedding
   has absolute value1; Kronecker's theorem makes it a root of unity.
6. For odd prime ell the root group is {+/-zeta^k}. The established primary
   condition J=1 mod(1-zeta)^2 identifies the correct one by testing
   A(1)=1, A'(1)=0 mod ell. This needs no quantum phase estimate.
7. Recover the at most (ell-1)^3 admissible sums, combine their explicit
   multiplicities and add p^2+p+1. No prime-square residue reconstruction or
   generic compact-output local division is needed on this classical route.

Each ideal contains p^2*A. Its canonical HNF basis has coefficient bit size
O(log p). The order has rank ell-1 and polynomial-size structure constants;
the whole theorem input has size polynomial in ell and log p. The output
also has polynomial size: writing J=sum_(j<ell-1) a_j*zeta^j, the known norm
implies ell*sum a_j^2-(sum a_j)^2=(ell-1)*p^2. The trace Gram's smallest
eigenvalue is1, so each |a_j|<=sqrt(ell-1)*p.

Thus enumeration of the character triples and root choices remains
polynomial in ell and log p. An explicit ell=poly(log p) promise suffices
for polynomial succinct-input time. Without it, neither the earlier quantum
proposal nor this reduction is claimed polynomial in log ell. This is a
complexity comparison, not an implementation/performance crossover claim.

## Independent Group-Ring Check

To avoid confusing the CM theorem with a generic-PIP solver, we also
construct an explicit input to the older Gentry-Szydlo setting.
[Lattices with Symmetry](https://arxiv.org/html/1501.00178), Remark 8.6,
explains the polynomial recovery of a generator from its ideal and cyclic
autocorrelation in R=Z[X]/(X^ell-1), ell odd prime.

Let J have canonical coefficients a_0,...,a_(ell-2), and pad a_(ell-1)=0.
Since sum a_j=1 mod ell and p=1 mod ell, the integer
c=(p-sum a_j)/ell exists. The lift v has coefficients a_j+c at all ell
positions. It projects to J and has augmentation v(1)=p.

The cyclic product v*bar(v)-p^2 vanishes in the cyclotomic quotient, so is
a multiple of Phi_ell in R. Its augmentation is0, hence that multiple is0.
Thus v has exactly known cyclic autocorrelation (p^2,0,...,0).

The public R-ideal imposes the SAME split-root carry constraints plus
augmentation divisible by p. Its index is p^(sum e_t+1)=p^ell. The principal
ideal (v) is contained in it and also has index
|v(1)*Norm_K(J)|=p^ell, proving equality. This proves the GS YES promise
without using v to construct the actual public basis.

For basis B, the normalized Gram B*B^T/p^2 is positive definite, integral
and unimodular. Cyclic shift has an explicit integral isometry matrix.
The cyclic order-2ell group is represented by -shift, whose ell-th power
is -I, matching the signed group-ring convention. Ordinary cyclotomic
trace Grams instead have determinant ell^(ell-2), NOT1; the two encodings
must not be silently interchanged. Group symmetry is supplied, not inferred
from an arbitrary unimodular lattice.

## Executed Evidence And Nonimplementation

Run:

```text
python theorems/jacobi_known_norm_reduction.py --write
python -m pytest -q tests/test_jacobi_known_norm_reduction.py tests/test_jacobi_surface_reconstruction.py
```

The producer builds both theorem inputs for six native controls and all51
distinct ideal profiles at p=2^61-1, ell11. It verifies exact product-ideal
HNF, normalized Gram positivity/determinants, module actions, signed cyclic
action, augmentation and index. The large inputs require no character
table, LLL, true Jacobi sum or phase estimate. The six small known-generator
lifts are separately charged CALIBRATIONS, not input constructors.
The reused reference source caps conductors at24 and primes below2^64;
these implementation caps are not assumptions of the symbolic reduction
or of the imported theorem, and exceeding them is not evidence of hardness.

Tests include an independent SymPy product-lattice HNF and matrix replay,
direct cyclic autocorrelations, all small admissible symmetric triples,
wrong norms, nonideal lattices with the right index, non-root unit
contamination and opposite-character conventions. A valid polarized input
is never labeled a solved instance just because those checks pass.

**Not executed:** the Lenstra-Silverberg auxiliary-ideal/tensor-power
generator-recovery algorithm. Existing actual surface reconstruction still
uses LLL plus exact primary normalization; its failure remains UNKNOWN for
that implementation. The asymptotic conclusion imports the published
classical theorem and depends on the stated local reduction proof, not on
finite success or a relabeling of LLL as GS. Local application has not had
independent human/formal review. No central candidate, proof or general
negative-result promotion is made automatically.

## Attempt To Falsify This Conclusion

- **Wrong theorem problem?** Theorem 1.3 requires the norm, not just the
  ideal. Here the norm is exactly the public scalar p^2. If the application
  supplied only an unknown positive unit times p^2, this reduction would
  fail. Native checks and the Jacobi Weil identity rule that out here.
- **Invalid ideal/involution?** Carry orientation matters. Every product
  ideal is checked exactly, and inverse-label inputs are retained as distinct
  valid inputs, not confused with the intended J. A carry or ideal-identity
  counterexample would invalidate the local application.
- **Norm identity implies existence?** It does not in general. This family
  has a concrete Jacobi witness analytically; arbitrary polarized ideals
  cannot inherit the YES conclusion. Native small witnesses independently
  check that premise but are not a proof for all inputs.
- **Uncharged number-theory oracle?** A verified eta is part of both input
  models; neither algorithm gets a hidden root for free. The imported
  theorem is unconditional deterministic polynomial time in its explicit
  input size, not a heuristic unit-group/PIP subroutine. Efficient public
  ideal construction and polynomial output size are shown above.
- **Root ambiguity still hard?** Prime-primary normalization removes it
  without evaluating J. This pass does NOT extend that step to all composite
  conductors. A counterexample to the prime-primary proof would reopen
  exact identification, not make generic normalized recovery quantum-hard.
- **Does this refute a recent quantum paper?** No. The repo's specific
  prime-conductor surface target is narrower than external claims and may
  have different output/input conventions. No author-error conclusion is
  inferred from a missing citation or this local reduction alone.

## Next Research Action

Retire this prime-conductor proposal as an asymptotic advantage target,
subject to independent review of the application. Keep its arithmetic
tests as reusable falsifiers. Do not spend main-model research budget
implementing a known GS algorithm solely to reproduce its theorem.

Before any broader arithmetic pivot, require a specific output NOT already
recoverable from a public ideal plus known relative norm. Otherwise compare
independent constructive mechanisms. Unknown norms or ambiguous composite
roots are not automatically hard tasks, and failure of LLL is not evidence
that a quantum algorithm is needed. A new candidate must have an explicit
end-to-end task and strongest known classical comparison first.

notes.title: Hermitian Qutrit Pilot: Actual Readout And Source-As-Solution Test
not_claimed: Local derivations, review pending; no novelty claim.
notes.result:
Can the known low-bond qudit pilot construction yield a noncommuting
Hamiltonian optimization algorithm that escapes the independent-qubit
radius solver and the existing classical OPI/polar competitors?

We first considered dependent-qubit wrappers. For H0 anticommuting with Q,
(H0+gQ)^2=H0^2+g^2 I; a wrapper alone transforms an existing spectrum, not
a new decoder. No dependent-code decoder was implemented or assumed here.
We instead changed the involution assumption: order-three Weyl generators
do not obey the preceding qubit square-root recurrence.

[Wocjan's pilot MPS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01022) applies to uniformly
twisted generators, including qudits.
[General-Pauli HDQI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18773)
separately charges source and decoding.
Neither supplies a ready Hermitian qutrit optimizer for the family below.

# Hermitian Qutrit Pilot: Actual Readout And Source-As-Solution Test

2026-10-17. Local derivations, review pending; no novelty claim.

## Scientific Question

Can the known low-bond qudit pilot construction yield a noncommuting
Hamiltonian optimization algorithm that escapes the independent-qubit
radius solver and the existing classical OPI/polar competitors?

We first considered dependent-qubit wrappers. For H0 anticommuting with Q,
(H0+gQ)^2=H0^2+g^2 I; a wrapper alone transforms an existing spectrum, not
a new decoder. No dependent-code decoder was implemented or assumed here.
We instead changed the involution assumption: order-three Weyl generators
do not obey the preceding qubit square-root recurrence.

[Wocjan's pilot MPS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01022) applies to uniformly
twisted generators, including qudits.
[General-Pauli HDQI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18773)
separately charges source and decoding.
Neither supplies a ready Hermitian qutrit optimizer for the family below.
Do not substitute a non-Hermitian free-parafermion spectrum for this task;
[Fendley's model](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.6049) explicitly distinguishes
the non-Hermitian setting. These references motivate a test, not a novelty
or hardness claim for our family.

## Explicit Problem And Proposed Mechanism

On m qutrits define X|b>=|b+1 mod3>, Z|b>=omega^b|b>, omega^2+omega+1=0,

    U_j = Z_0 ... Z_(j-1) X_j,
    H = sum_j c_j (U_j + U_j^dagger),       c_j explicit signed integers.

This is an explicit physical many-body family, not a hidden oracle. X
pivots make the U_j labels independent over F3. Ordered products E_r
(r in F3^m) are Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal. Decoding their labels is linear:
x_j=r_j, z_j=sum_(l>j)r_l; no unknown low-weight decoder is supplied.

Proposed algorithm: prepare coefficients alpha_r(P(H)) as a pilot state,
apply public label SUMs and a tensor-product qutrit Bell transform, then
discard the reference half. For Hermitian real P this gives P(H)^2/Tr(P(H)^2).
Use P=(t-H)^k, t=2 sum|c_j|, rather than H^(2k) which need not favor low
energies. A major advantage would require a polynomial source AND a charged
degree/gap/overlap argument beyond the best classical baseline. None is
assumed. The native source uses exponential exact coefficient enumeration
and charged TT-SVD; those are calibration tools, NOT the proposed algorithm.

## Result 1: Hermitian Completion Breaks The Direct Pilot Transfer

For A=sum c_j U_j, the one-directional relation gives A^3=(sum c_j^3)I.
The small source has low-degree algebra, but A is non-Hermitian. Adding
U_j^dagger introduces both omega and omega^-1 commutations and a commuting
inverse partner for each generator. With at least two noncommuting pairs,
no generator is uniform against all remaining predecessors: there is no
valid last vertex for that theorem's ordering.

The degree-two Hermitian coefficient tensor on c=[2,3,5,7], cut2, has a4x4
minor with EXACT determinant -4200-8400*omega, nonzero in Z[omega]. Thus the
bond bound degree+1=3 cannot be copied to this natural grouped-site pilot.
The corresponding one-directional power has rank3. This rejects a precise
transfer claim, not all polynomial bonds, site reorderings, gauge changes
or efficient non-MPS quantum source circuits.

Higher controls retain all initial six/eight-site exploratory inputs through
degree10, including saturation. They are exact modular lower-bound witnesses
(omega maps to5 mod31), not fitted exponents or rank upper bounds. All56
records retain coefficients, degree, cut, selected rows/columns, the minor
and its nonzero determinant. No asymptotic rank fit or hardness inference
is performed. The degree-two determinant is additionally evaluated directly
in characteristic zero, independently of numerical SVD.

## Result 2: Readout Actually Works

Exact coefficient multiplication uses

    E_r U_j^s = omega^(s*sum_(l>j)r_l) E_(r+s e_j),   s=+1,-1.

No floating phase is used by this expansion. The native readout starts from
the pilot and zero ancillas, computes the public z labels, applies one
qutrit Fourier per reference coordinate, and then coordinatewise SUM. It
does NOT use one cyclic Fourier over dimension3^m. It uses
m(m-1)/2+2m ideal logical qutrit Clifford gates; no fault-tolerant compilation
is claimed. Three full-state controls compare the prepared purification to
vec(P(H))/norm(P(H)) and its energy to dense physical matrices. All sources
and exponential transition counts are retained. Merely getting the label
law right would not pass these checks.

## Result 3: The Source Is Already The Filtered Seed State

E_r|0>=|r>. Therefore alpha(P(H))=P(H)|0>, not a freely supplied string of
coefficients. Since <0|E_r|0>=Tr(E_r)/3^m, this seed is a trace vector for
the generated algebra. More strongly, left multiplication obeys

    U_j E_r = omega^(sum_(i<j)r_i) E_(r+e_j),

exactly the SAME prefix-Weyl action on the pilot coordinates. The Bell
isometry intertwines H on the pilot and H on the physical output. Thus for
ANY normalized pilot, input and output have identical energy expectations.
Native tests check this for actual filters AND arbitrary entangled pilots.
Constructing a high-quality quantum pilot could still be an algorithm, but
the decoder/readout has not removed its hard preparation step. This is not
a general assertion that all HDQI or quantum state preparation is circular.

## Result 4: A Matched Classical MPS Competitor

Given an actual supplied pilot MPS A_j[r] of bondD, pair the output a_j and
reference b_j at each site. Track s=sum_(i<j)b_i mod3 and use

    T_j[(alpha,s),(a,b),(beta,s+b)]
      = A_j[alpha,a-b,beta] * omega^((a-b)*s) / sqrt(3).

Its product-Weyl energy is contractible classically. Even more directly,

same mean without any output construction. Hence a constructible polynomial-
bond controlled-precision pilot cannot support an ENERGY-estimation
separation here. This does not claim the unknown optimum energy is easy.

A live64-site product-pilot control executes the charge construction and
both energy contractions, checked by an independent scalar product formula.

against full arrays. Floating contractions/SVDs are not interval certificates;
controlled precision and constructibility remain premises of the asymptotic
classical comparison. No general measurement or non-MPS dequantization follows.

## Decision And Next Experiment

Run `python theorems/hermitian_qutrit_pilot.py --write` and
`python -m pytest tests/test_hermitian_qutrit_pilot.py -q`.

Do not implement the known one-directional pilot formula as if it already
prepared a physical Hermitian optimizer. Do not declare growing finite
ranks a quantum advantage. Do not compile a low-bond pilot to claim an
energy speedup already matched by these contractions.

The surviving scientific question is an explicit efficiently constructible
NON-MPS source or a code-aware, dependent-label mechanism whose actual
readout is not this finite-charge contraction. Any proposal must name that
source/decoder and its polynomial filter/gap guarantee before a new
subsystem. Further degree/site-size scans do not resolve this blocker.
No central candidate, general negative, proof promotion or novelty claim.

derivations.heading: Local Radius Derivation
derivations.text:
Set H_j=sum_(i<=j) c_i P_i and R_j=norm(H_j). Independence gives two facts:

1. No nonempty product of these Pauli labels is the identity. In particular,
   tr(P_j f(H_(j-1)))=0 for every polynomial f when P_j commutes with all
   previous terms. Each eigenspace of H_(j-1) therefore has equal +1/-1
   multiplicities for P_j (spectral projectors are finite polynomials).
2. A Pauli Q anticommuting with every P_i exists: solve the full-row-rank
   symplectic system with all-one right-hand side. Thus every H_j has a
   spectrum symmetric about zero. This is not assumed for dependent labels.

If P_j commutes with all predecessors, both independent sign sectors occur:

    R_j = R_(j-1) + abs(c_j).

If it anticommutes with all predecessors, cross terms cancel:

    H_j^2 = H_(j-1)^2 + c_j^2 I,
    R_j = sqrt(R_(j-1)^2 + c_j^2).

Starting from R_0=0 gives E_min=-R_m. This is an O(m)-operation scalar
expression after polynomial-time rank/order validation. Bit complexity is
polynomial in input length and log(1/epsilon): use outward dyadic square-root
rounding with b>=ceil(log2(m/epsilon)). Each root is monotone and 1-Lipschitz
as a function of nonnegative previous radius, so interval width is at most
(number of root steps)*2^(-b). The executable solver uses integer square
roots and Fractions, never a numerical eigensolver, to produce the enclosure.

This falsifies the proposed ground-ENERGY separation, not HDQI correctness,
Gibbs sampling, arbitrary computational-basis sampling or quantum outputs.

state. No unsupported output-sampling equivalence is inferred.

notes.text:
# Independent-Label Hamiltonian DQI: Constructive Test And Classical Falsifier

2026-10-17. Local derivation, review pending; no novelty claim.

## Question And Selection

Can a noncommuting Pauli family combine efficient HDQI pilot preparation and
trivial syndrome decoding into a substantial ENERGY optimization advantage?

This is independent of the recent DCP obstruction batch. We compared:

- Further DCP readout variations: no new end-to-end construction identified.
- Hermitian-code DQI: a real extension of the code family, but not by itself a
  solution to compact predicate preparation or the existing classical attacks.
  See [Gu and Jordan](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06603).
- General-Pauli HDQI: separates pilot-state preparation from decoding.
  [Bu, Gu and Li](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18773) give a conditional algorithm.
  [Wocjan](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01022) gives efficient pilot MPSs when
  each generator has a uniform commutation sign against its predecessors.
  That paper explicitly leaves useful jointly decodable families open.

We selected the third route because independent symplectic labels remove
the decoding premise by binary linear inversion. That makes the proposed
family falsifiable without implementing an assumed decoder oracle.

## Concrete Proposed Family

Input is an explicit list of Hermitian Pauli words P_j and signed rational
coefficients c_j, H=sum_j c_j P_j. No unknown oracle, random function, QRAM
table or hidden advice is supplied. The symplectic labels must be linearly
independent over F2. A verified ordering must make P_j either commute with
ALL preceding words or anticommute with ALL of them. Repeated/identity/
dependent labels are rejected; unsupported graphs mean UNKNOWN, not hard.

Canonical physical realizations on m qubits are:

    P_j = X_j                      (commuting addition)
    P_j = Z_0 ... Z_(j-1) X_j       (anticommuting addition).

The X pivot on each new qubit proves independence. A last anticommuting
addition can connect all m terms, so this is not merely a bounded-component
test. The saved m512 control has that property.

Proposed quantum mechanism: known predecessor-uniform pilot MPS, reversible
linear syndrome inversion, coherent Bell readout and a suitable polynomial
filter. A polynomial-time ground-energy algorithm could matter only if
the same explicit family resists classical optimum-energy computation.
Pilot theorem, polynomial degree, precision, normalization and readout must
all be charged; a preparation subroutine alone never proves a speedup.

## Local Radius Derivation

Set H_j=sum_(i<=j) c_i P_i and R_j=norm(H_j). Independence gives two facts:

1. No nonempty product of these Pauli labels is the identity. In particular,
   tr(P_j f(H_(j-1)))=0 for every polynomial f when P_j commutes with all
   previous terms. Each eigenspace of H_(j-1) therefore has equal +1/-1
   multiplicities for P_j (spectral projectors are finite polynomials).
2. A Pauli Q anticommuting with every P_i exists: solve the full-row-rank
   symplectic system with all-one right-hand side. Thus every H_j has a
   spectrum symmetric about zero. This is not assumed for dependent labels.

If P_j commutes with all predecessors, both independent sign sectors occur:

    R_j = R_(j-1) + abs(c_j).

If it anticommutes with all predecessors, cross terms cancel:

    H_j^2 = H_(j-1)^2 + c_j^2 I,
    R_j = sqrt(R_(j-1)^2 + c_j^2).

Starting from R_0=0 gives E_min=-R_m. This is an O(m)-operation scalar
expression after polynomial-time rank/order validation. Bit complexity is
polynomial in input length and log(1/epsilon): use outward dyadic square-root
rounding with b>=ceil(log2(m/epsilon)). Each root is monotone and 1-Lipschitz
as a function of nonnegative previous radius, so interval width is at most
(number of root steps)*2^(-b). The executable solver uses integer square
roots and Fractions, never a numerical eigensolver, to produce the enclosure.

This falsifies the proposed ground-ENERGY separation, not HDQI correctness,
Gibbs sampling, arbitrary computational-basis sampling or quantum outputs.
The classical task here is to compute an optimum energy, not emit a quantum
state. No unsupported output-sampling equivalence is inferred.

## Constructive Native Ground-State Check

The canonical family also has a direct recursive ground circuit. An isolated
addition appends the correct X eigenstate. An anticommuting addition appends
|0> and applies exp(-i theta Z_<j Y_j/2), theta=-atan2(c_j,R_(j-1)). The two
basis vectors are the old ground state tensored with0, and its Z_<j image
tensored with1; H_j restricts to [[-R,c],[c,R]]. The rotation prepares its
lower eigenvector. Each Pauli rotation has an O(j)-gate elementary
decomposition, yielding a polynomial canonical construction without HDQI.
Only bounded dense execution is implemented; no native Clifford transport
to a general input realization or compiled fault-tolerant circuit is claimed.

## Evidence And Scope Falsifiers

Run `python theorems/hdqi_predecessor_uniform.py --write` and
`python -m pytest tests/test_hdqi_predecessor_uniform.py -q`.

- Four saved native Hamiltonians retain every term/coefficient, discovered
  order, rational enclosure, dense smallest eigenvalue and executed ground
  state's eigenvector residual. Tests check every predecessor pattern up to
  five terms, signed/zero coefficients, Y terms and smaller realizations.
- All120 input permutations of a mixed five-term example check order search.
- Independent high-precision Decimal arithmetic checks rational enclosures.
- A512-term input has a live rank/order/rational certificate, NOT a dense
  quantum run or evidence of a speedup.
- Dependence matters: ZZI+IZZ+ZIZ has ground energy-1, not-3. Its labels sum
  to zero; the API rejects it. A path-P4 commutation graph is also rejected,
  without claiming hardness or integrability failure.

## Decision And Next Experiment

Do not compile HDQI or run larger parameter scans on the independent-label
predecessor-uniform family to claim an ENERGY advantage. The strongest
baseline is the radius solver, not annealing or a generic exponential method.
The local proof still needs independent mathematical review and prior-art
comparison; no central proof status or broad negative has been promoted.

A surviving proposal must specify dependent labels with a real polynomial
decoder and nontrivial optimization task, or a different pilot preparation
on a graph outside this condition. For dependent labels, first compute
actual product/central constraints and test the decoder's promised radius;
do not retain the independent sign-sector argument. For a sampling claim,
specify the accessible observable/output and a matched classical sampling
task separately. These are scientific requirements, not requests to build
another general research subsystem.

notes.title: Explicit Cubic-Target OPI: A Structural Classical Falsifier
not_claimed: No new quantum algorithm, hardness proof, oracle problem or admitted speedup candidate.
notes.result:
Does replacing quadratic targets by public cubic circuits remove the large
accepted affine flats exploited by the previous classical attack, or does a
constructive polarization attack still erase the finite mean-score comparison?
The previous quadratic result was progress, not a reason to keep varying its
seeds. Dense symmetric cubics are not an escape: e3=e1*e2 in the Boolean ring.

Input: a scalar Reed-Solomon evaluation code of dimension K at the distinct
nonzero field elements represented by integers 1,...,N in F_(2^t), with
N <= 2^t-1. The FLINT irreducible polynomial and coefficient basis are saved.
Each position supplies a public invertible binary matrix T_i and a public
Boolean polynomial g_i in t-1 variables of degree AT MOST three:

```
z = T_i y
accept_i(y) iff z0 = g_i(z1,...,z[t-1]).
```

All constant, linear, quadratic and cubic coefficients are sampled. Degenerate
polynomials, bad attack attempts and all predeclared sources are retained.
Balance is exact for every input, not a typical-source assertion. The input
description is O(N t^3) bits; classical and quantum algorithms see the SAME
description. No membership table, hidden advice or hard oracle is supplied.
In particular t=31,N=31 does not require materializing a 2^31-entry predicate.

controls.heading: Stronger Classical Attack
controls.text:
For a Boolean cubic g, the third finite difference
T(v,w,a)=Delta_v Delta_w Delta_a g is an alternating trilinear form.

1. Build independent directions v_1,...,v_d with T zero on every triple.
   Each extension is a Gaussian nullspace problem: T(v_i,v_j,v)=0.
2. Solve LINEAR affine-base equations
   T(v_i,v_j,a)=Delta_vi Delta_vj g(0). Inconsistent bases trigger charged
   retries and then smaller dimension. They are not an OPI UNSAT result.
3. The restriction g(a+sum s_i v_i) is now affine. Lift its graph to an
   accepted d-flat in the transformed symbol coordinates. Check EVERY point
   in this small flat, derive its parity checks, and compose with the actual
   binary RS evaluation map.
4. Interpolate inside successive accepted flats using exact binary Gaussian
   elimination. Keep all failures; never select a favorable new source.
5. On the remaining affine message space, recover each restricted degree-3
   polynomial by at most sum_(j<=3) C(d_free,j) evaluations. A Boolean Mobius
   transform evaluates all 2^d_free messages. Optimize the full native score,
   not merely the forced prefix. Verify the winner with independent FLINT
   Horner evaluation, not the binary surrogate used by the optimizer.

All contractions, flat polynomial evaluations, Gaussian solves, residual
candidates, transform XOR cells, table storage and native checks are exposed.
The residual enumeration is exponential in d_free, not a free polynomial-time
subroutine. Caps return UNKNOWN with a verified uniform affine fallback.
There is no maximum-flat, global optimum, mixing or attack-success theorem.
The default requested local dimension obeys C(d,2)+d <= t-1; this avoids
assuming a generically full-rank base system where rank is impossible.

Finding constant/low-degree restrictions is established prior art, not a new
idea: [Cohen and Tal, Sections 3-4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.0654), and
[Boyar and Find, algebraic thickness and normality](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.1318).
The implementation here directly exploits the public cubic tensor and graph
lift; no claim that it improves those theorems is made.

```

python -m pytest tests/test_explicit_cubic_opi.py -q -W error::RuntimeWarning
```

Predeclared controls: (t,N,K)=(4,7,3),(15,31,9),(31,31,9),(31,127,39),
seeds 29 and 71, four paid attacks each. The first is an exact calibration,
not an algorithmic result. Saved specifications permit native witness replay.

Falsifiers: verified classical scores erase the claimed mean-score target;
larger native flats or residual optimizers make the finite comparison easy;
or the apparent quantum route needs uncharged preparation/readout work.
Absence of a successful attack is NOT a hardness certificate. Even beating
these classical implementations would leave matched resources, tail laws,
stronger classical algorithms and an actual quantum implementation unresolved.
notes.decision:
Do not spend main-model research on more seed/degree/field-size scans. The
concrete next classical challenge is a code-aware NONLINEAR repair that can
change pools using the remaining predicates, rather than paying exponentially
for a released large flat. The quantum challenge is a charged decoder/filter
resource analysis and a matched tail comparison, not a new oracle promise.
Compare that work against independent constructive directions before extending
this line. CLI wiring and production-wide regression are mechanical follow-up;
no central candidate admission, generic negative result or proof promotion.

# Explicit Cubic-Target OPI: A Structural Classical Falsifier

2026-10-17. Local derivations, review pending. No new quantum algorithm,
hardness proof, oracle problem or admitted speedup candidate.

## Scientific Question

Does replacing quadratic targets by public cubic circuits remove the large
accepted affine flats exploited by the previous classical attack, or does a
constructive polarization attack still erase the finite mean-score comparison?
The previous quadratic result was progress, not a reason to keep varying its
seeds. Dense symmetric cubics are not an escape: e3=e1*e2 in the Boolean ring.

Input: a scalar Reed-Solomon evaluation code of dimension K at the distinct
nonzero field elements represented by integers 1,...,N in F_(2^t), with
N <= 2^t-1. The FLINT irreducible polynomial and coefficient basis are saved.
Each position supplies a public invertible binary matrix T_i and a public
Boolean polynomial g_i in t-1 variables of degree AT MOST three:

```
z = T_i y
accept_i(y) iff z0 = g_i(z1,...,z[t-1]).
```

All constant, linear, quadratic and cubic coefficients are sampled. Degenerate
polynomials, bad attack attempts and all predeclared sources are retained.
Balance is exact for every input, not a typical-source assertion. The input
description is O(N t^3) bits; classical and quantum algorithms see the SAME
description. No membership table, hidden advice or hard oracle is supplied.
In particular t=31,N=31 does not require materializing a 2^31-entry predicate.

## Constructive Quantum Route And Its Limits

Use the KNOWN balanced-DQI polynomial filter and conventional coherent unique
decoding of the RS dual. Each local Boolean phase is implementable by public
linear gates and bounded-control monomial gates, with O(t^3) predicate work.
An indexed implementation can scan the public descriptions in polynomial
work; no unit-cost QRAM is assumed. Field arithmetic, support preparation,
decoder reversibility and precision must all be charged in an actual circuit.
The retained degree ell obeys the STRICT condition 2 ell+1 < K+1.

The existing rational-filter score enclosure is reused for finite comparisons.
The known optimal layered mean approaches 1/2+sqrt((R/2)(1-R/2)) at fixed
rate R=K/N when ell/N approaches R/2; this is not an asymptotic certification
of the implementation's fixed-denominator rational rounding convention.
This is a known constructive theoretical target, NOT our executed circuit or
certified resource advantage. A major computational separation would require
classical hardness for this explicit family, not the random-oracle theorem.
No such hardness evidence exists here. A best-of-four classical score versus
a one-shot quantum mean is NOT a matched time/tail comparison.

Primary reference: [balanced folded DQI, score law and phase implementation,
Appendix A](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02145v2#A1). Its oracle lower bound is
not transferred to these compact predicates.

## Stronger Classical Attack

For a Boolean cubic g, the third finite difference
T(v,w,a)=Delta_v Delta_w Delta_a g is an alternating trilinear form.

1. Build independent directions v_1,...,v_d with T zero on every triple.
   Each extension is a Gaussian nullspace problem: T(v_i,v_j,v)=0.
2. Solve LINEAR affine-base equations
   T(v_i,v_j,a)=Delta_vi Delta_vj g(0). Inconsistent bases trigger charged
   retries and then smaller dimension. They are not an OPI UNSAT result.
3. The restriction g(a+sum s_i v_i) is now affine. Lift its graph to an
   accepted d-flat in the transformed symbol coordinates. Check EVERY point
   in this small flat, derive its parity checks, and compose with the actual
   binary RS evaluation map.
4. Interpolate inside successive accepted flats using exact binary Gaussian
   elimination. Keep all failures; never select a favorable new source.
5. On the remaining affine message space, recover each restricted degree-3
   polynomial by at most sum_(j<=3) C(d_free,j) evaluations. A Boolean Mobius
   transform evaluates all 2^d_free messages. Optimize the full native score,
   not merely the forced prefix. Verify the winner with independent FLINT
   Horner evaluation, not the binary surrogate used by the optimizer.

All contractions, flat polynomial evaluations, Gaussian solves, residual
candidates, transform XOR cells, table storage and native checks are exposed.
The residual enumeration is exponential in d_free, not a free polynomial-time
subroutine. Caps return UNKNOWN with a verified uniform affine fallback.
There is no maximum-flat, global optimum, mixing or attack-success theorem.
The default requested local dimension obeys C(d,2)+d <= t-1; this avoids
assuming a generically full-rank base system where rank is impossible.

Finding constant/low-degree restrictions is established prior art, not a new
idea: [Cohen and Tal, Sections 3-4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.0654), and
[Boyar and Find, algebraic thickness and normality](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.1318).
The implementation here directly exploits the public cubic tensor and graph
lift; no claim that it improves those theorems is made.

## Why The Quadratic Rank Argument Does Not Automatically Transfer

For an IID uniform RM(3,t-1) coefficient vector, its restriction to any
d-dimensional base flat is a uniform RM(3,d) polynomial. A graph-flat projects
injectively to a base flat, and there are 2^(d+1) possible affine graph heights.
Thus, with [m choose d]_2 the exact Gaussian binomial and
D3(d)=sum_(j=0)^min(3,d) C(d,j), the first moment gives

```
Pr(any accepted d-flat among N predicates)
 <= min(1, N * 2^t * [t-1 choose d]_2 * 2^(-D3(d))).
```

This counts ARBITRARY affine flats, not just the constructor's restricted
search. Invertible T_i preserve dimensions. For sufficiently large t, a
constant-fraction-dimensional flat is unlikely in the stated coefficient
ensemble. This is only a geometric obstruction to the previous attack's
particular large-flat premise. It does NOT prove OPI hardness or eliminate
nonlinear, global, decoding, differential or code-aware classical algorithms.
The seeded examples are not IID probability certificates. Small t=3,d=2 is
independently calibrated against all sixteen Boolean polynomials.

## Execution And Falsifiers

```
python theorems/explicit_cubic_opi.py --write
python -m pytest tests/test_explicit_cubic_opi.py -q -W error::RuntimeWarning
```

Predeclared controls: (t,N,K)=(4,7,3),(15,31,9),(31,31,9),(31,127,39),
seeds 29 and 71, four paid attacks each. The first is an exact calibration,
not an algorithmic result. Saved specifications permit native witness replay.

Falsifiers: verified classical scores erase the claimed mean-score target;
larger native flats or residual optimizers make the finite comparison easy;
or the apparent quantum route needs uncharged preparation/readout work.
Absence of a successful attack is NOT a hardness certificate. Even beating
these classical implementations would leave matched resources, tail laws,
stronger classical algorithms and an actual quantum implementation unresolved.

## Live Results

Both seeds retained, four paid attempts each:

| t,N,K | Best classical scores, seeds 29/71 | Known chosen-filter mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4,7,3 | 7/7, 7/7 | 0.688982 |
| 15,31,9 | 27/31, 27/31 | 0.747358 |
| 31,31,9 | 30/31, 30/31 | 0.747358 |
| 31,127,39 | 105/127, 104/127 | 0.816830 |

At 127 positions each attempt forces 50 accepted predicates, leaves nine
free bits, and exactly optimizes 512 residual messages. At t=31,N=31 it
forces eleven predicates and enumerates 32,768 messages per attempt. All
32 attempts finish below the residual cap; every attempt and native witness
is saved, not just the winners. Flat construction and four-trial selection
are charged. There is no finite best-score advantage in these comparisons,
but the test has NOT matched quantum repetition, tails or runtime.

## Why This Does Not Settle The Asymptotic Question

The producer also records a scoped exact IID-model tail bound. Suppose the
union of candidate message pools is determined using only the first E
predicate polynomials, BEFORE the remaining scores are seen, and has at most
S messages. Uniform independent suffix constants make each fixed message's
suffix score Binomial(N-E,1/2). Whatever dependencies exist BETWEEN messages,

```
Pr(best pool score >= k) <= min(1, S * Pr(Binomial(N-E,1/2) >= k-E)).
```

Allow all exposed predicates a free success. The maximum stopping prefix
over the fixed four attacks is a stopping time; conditioning on that prefix
leaves the suffix polynomials independent. Residual optimization may use all
suffix scores to SELECT a winner, but may not change the previously fixed
pool. Unused terminal flats and failed interpolations count as exposed.
This is not an empirical confidence bound for seeded sources. At the present
sizes it can be vacuous; that is recorded rather than converted to hardness.

Conditional asymptotic interpretation: if E/N -> R and log S=o(N), this attack
cannot beat (1+R)/2 by a constant with nonvanishing IID-model probability.
For 0<R<1 the known DQI target is strictly above that limit, since
R/2-R^2/4 > R^2/4. The premise is plausible for a full-rank prefix of flats
of dimension O(sqrt(t)), with t=Theta(log N) and polynomial-sized residual
pools. A uniform constructor/rank analysis and an extension beyond this
reference's finite field/dimension caps are NOT supplied. If many failures
expose most predicates or a new repair adapts pools using suffix information,
the premise fails and this bound cannot be used against that algorithm.

Thus the observed finite win does not prove asymptotic dequantization, and
an asymptotic weakness of THIS pool would not prove classical hardness.
Both mistakes would manufacture a result from the same limited evidence.

## Next Decision

Do not spend main-model research on more seed/degree/field-size scans. The
concrete next classical challenge is a code-aware NONLINEAR repair that can
change pools using the remaining predicates, rather than paying exponentially
for a released large flat. The quantum challenge is a charged decoder/filter
resource analysis and a matched tail comparison, not a new oracle promise.
Compare that work against independent constructive directions before extending
this line. CLI wiring and production-wide regression are mechanical follow-up;
no central candidate admission, generic negative result or proof promotion.
